testResults.name: Identifier can't start with a digit

viva.summary: The student understands the purpose of the DFA simulation and can explain key parts of the code, but mispredicted the output for a test case. They correctly described how to modify the function for undefined transitions.

rubric.revise_next: Review how the DIV3 DFA processes each input symbol so you can predict its acceptance results accurately.

questions.answer: It checks if the pair (current state, next character) is listed as a rule in the transition table, so the machine knows where to go. If it isn't there, the code just stops the machine and says it can't read that input, because the DFA doesn't allow that step.
questions.feedback: Good explanation of the transition‑check; it shows you know why the DFA must verify the key before moving.
questions.prompt: In your `run_dfa` function, what does the line `if key in dfa['delta']:` do, and why is this check necessary for the DFA simulation?

questions.feedback: The prediction is incorrect; the DFA actually accepts '0' for DIV3.
questions.prompt: What does the call `accepts(DIV3, '0')` return when executed with your code?

questions.answer: I would change the else branch to set current_state = current_state instead of returning None, so the DFA just stays in the same state when it sees an unknown symbol. Then the function would keep going without getting stuck.
questions.feedback: Your suggested change correctly keeps the machine in the same state for unknown symbols.
questions.prompt: Suppose we want `run_dfa` to treat any character not present in the transition table as causing the DFA to stay in the same state instead of getting stuck. How would you modify your function to implement this behavior?

messages.body: I got an error when I ran it. Which line should I look at first?

It looks like a small typo in the variable name is causing the NameError. Take a close look at the last line of your function and compare it with your initialization. Can you spot the difference in spelling?
messages.hint: Check if the variable name in the return statement matches exactly with the one you defined earlier.
